This does not influence our rankings or medical evaluations. Fatigue that sleep does not fix. A libido that has quietly disappeared. Brain fog, irritability, and a body that no longer responds to the gym the way it used to. These can be symptoms of low testosterone 1 , a condition that affects up to 13.8 million men in the United States 2 . Yet many men never receive a diagnosis or treatment. Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) has been a recognized treatment for clinically low testosterone for decades 3 . What has changed is access. Telehealth platforms now allow patients to consult with licensed clinicians, complete lab work, and receive prescribed medications without visiting a traditional urology or endocrinology office. But the market is noisy. Dozens of online TRT clinics compete for attention, each promising transparent pricing, expert care, and fast results. The reality is more complicated. Pricing structures vary dramatically, from flat monthly subscriptions to pay-per-service models where the true cost only becomes clear after multiple appointments. Some clinics prescribe FDA-approved testosterone, while others rely on compounded formulations from partner pharmacies. Cancellation policies range from genuinely flexible to effectively non-refundable. And not every provider requires the lab work and ongoing monitoring that safe TRT demands. Here, we’ll look at five online TRT providers: Male Excel, Peter MD, Hone Health, Fountain TRT, and Defy Medical. We’ll cover verified pricing, medication formats, clinical oversight, cancellation policies, fees that may not be obvious upfront, and real customer feedback. The goal is not to declare a winner, but to give you the specific details you need to make an informed decision based on your priorities. Quick Picks Best overall provider: Male Excel Best for beginners: Hone Health Best for flexible care: Defy Medical Best value: PeterMD Best for concierge support: Fountain TRT Male Excel earns the overall confidence pick because it combines BBB accreditation with an A+ rating, a 4.6-star Trustpilot rating across 4,772+ reviews, publishes membership and starting medication prices, but final cost depends on dose, a daily microdosing protocol that differentiates it from weekly-injection competitors, unlimited provider access, and a 90-day Excel Advantage Guarantee. Hone Health also holds BBB A+ accreditation and a larger Trustpilot review base. The providers reviewed here excel in different areas, so scores reflect strengths within each care model rather than a single universal ranking. For more insight on how our team vets, qualifies, and ranks providers, review our full methodology here . TRT Formats: Injections, Creams, Gels, and More Online clinics typically offer injectable testosterone cypionate, which is the most common format. Some also offer topical creams, gels, pellets, nasal gels, or oral therapies 3 . Cream and gel are not the same product. Creams are typically compounded, while gels are more often FDA-approved formulations like AndroGel 3,4 . Not every clinic offers every format, and availability often depends on what their partner pharmacy compounds. FDA-Approved vs. Compounded Testosterone FDA-approved testosterone products have undergone formal regulatory review for safety and efficacy 5 . Compounded medications are mixed by specialty pharmacies for individual patients and are not FDA-approved. Compounded products are widely used when clinically appropriate, but they are not equivalent to FDA-approved products in terms of regulatory review. Ask your provider which type you are receiving. Pricing Transparency Advertised monthly prices rarely tell the whole story. Some clinics bundle labs, consultations, and medication into one fee. Others charge separately for each component. Entry costs, lab processing fees, and medication costs can add $50 to $200 per month on top of a base subscription. Always calculate the true all-in monthly cost before committing. Clinical Oversight Any reputable TRT provider requires blood work before prescribing and at regular intervals afterward. Look for clinics that mandate labs at least every six months, offer video consultations with licensed physicians or mid-level providers, and adjust dosing based on lab results rather than symptoms alone. Cancellation and Refund Policies Some clinics allow cancellation at any time. Others require multi-month commitments or auto-renew with short notice windows. Shipped medications are also generally non-refundable. Read the fine print before entering payment information. Red Flags Here are red flags to look out for with any potential TRT provider: Before you sign up: Legitimate providers should be transparent from the start. Use caution if a clinic does not clearly disclose pricing before onboarding, does not identify its prescribing clinicians, or makes specific outcome guarantees. Before your first prescription: A reputable TRT provider should require baseline bloodwork before prescribing testosterone. Baseline testing commonly includes total testosterone, and may include free testosterone, LH, FSH, hematocrit/CBC, PSA when age- or risk-appropriate, and other labs based on the clinician’s judgment. Be equally wary of clinics that skip a real clinical consultation. If the process relies only on an asynchronous questionnaire without clear clinician review, that may be a sign to ask more questions before proceeding. After you’re a patient: Red flags here include no scheduled follow-up labs to monitor hematocrit, estradiol, and PSA (which can be affected by TRT); no discussion of risks or contraindications; and early promotion of add-ons like HCG, peptides, or other compounds before your baseline treatment plan is established. A trustworthy TRT provider treats ongoing monitoring as a core part of treatment. 1. Male Excel: Daily Microdosing With a Membership Model Best For: Patients interested in a daily microdosing TRT protocol Our Score: 4.5/5 | Trustpilot: 4.6★ (4,772 reviews) Overview Male Excel centers its TRT program on a daily microdosing model, either daily injections or daily testosterone cream, marketed as a way to support steadier testosterone levels than traditional weekly injection protocols. Unlike many competitors, Male Excel publishes the components of its pricing upfront, though the final cost still depends on your prescribed dosage. On Trustpilot, Male Excel holds a 4.6-star rating across 4,772 reviews at the time of writing. The BBB lists Male Excel as accredited with an A+ rating, with 38 complaints filed in the last 3 years (16 closed in the last 12 months). Patients praise the daily microdosing approach and unlimited provider access. Complaints tend to focus on shipping/billing issues and inconsistent communication after onboarding. The trade-off: Male Excel offers a differentiated clinical protocol, transparent baseline pricing, and strong BBB credentials, but the membership-plus-medication structure means you’re paying $99/month even in months when you don’t need active care, and patients are locked into Male Excel’s contracted pharmacies. You cannot transfer your prescription to a local pharmacy. Peter MD : Transparent All-Inclusive Pricing With a Broad Medication Menu Best For: Patients who want predictable monthly costs and a wide range of treatment options Our Score: 4.4/5 | Trustpilot: 4.7★ (13,968+ reviews) Overview Peter MD offers one of the more transparent pricing models among the providers reviewed here. The all-inclusive subscription bundles medication, labs, and consultations into a single monthly fee, with commitment-tier discounts that bring costs as low as $79/mo on an annual plan. The checkout process is notably upfront about what is and is not included. Peter MD previously displayed a 4.7-star Trustpilot rating across more than 13,968 reviews, the largest review volume among the providers on this list. Positive reviews commonly cited a straightforward onboarding process, responsive customer support, and access to a broad range of treatment options, including testosterone cypionate, enclomiphene, anastrozole, HCG, peptides, and growth hormone. However, at the time of review, Peter MD’s Trustpilot profile had been removed and was no longer publicly accessible. Trustpilot states that removed profiles are taken down when a business is found to be in violation of its guidelines, although additional details were not publicly provided. As far as BBB is concerned, Peter MD is not BBB accredited and has a 3.4/5 average across a small number of customer reviews. Some complaints describe delayed or unfulfilled orders, refund issues, and medication received at or near expiration. These concerns do not necessarily mean most customers have a negative experience, but they are worth weighing carefully alongside Peter MD’s prior large volume of positive Trustpilot reviews, especially for patients considering multi-month discounted plans. The trade-off: For patients who value predictable monthly costs, Peter MD is one of the clearer options reviewed here, with a broader medication menu than many competitors. However, the lack of BBB accreditation and the nature of some publicly posted complaints may give cautious consumers reason to review the terms, refund policy, and recent customer feedback carefully before enrolling. Hone Health : Guided Onboarding With a Tiered Subscription Best For: Men new to TRT who want a structured, step-by-step process Our Score: 4.2/5| Trustpilot: 4.8★ (11,150+ reviews) Overview The primary concern with Hone Health is that the true all-in monthly cost for TRT is not disclosed until after you complete labs and a consultation. Hone’s advertised $25/month Basic tier is often mistaken for the TRT entry point, but it’s actually a longevity and lab-testing membership that does not include hormone therapy. The actual TRT tier is Plus at $129/month, which starts at $174 to cover initial labs and your first month. Premium runs $149/month and starts at $214. Medication costs are billed separately and vary based on dosage and modality. The Plus TRT tier includes 9 initial biomarkers, while the Premium tier includes 50+ 6 . On Trustpilot, Hone holds a 4.8-star rating across more than 11,150 reviews. Users consistently praise the at-home lab kits, the ease of the onboarding process, and the quality of clinician consultations. Hone is also BBB accredited with an A+ rating, though BBB complaints reveal a different theme: billing disputes, charges after cancellation, and unresponsive customer service. The clinical experience tends to be strong; billing and support issues appear to be the main themes in negative complaints. The trade-off is clear: Hone offers one of the smoothest onboarding experiences in the market, but you pay a premium for that convenience, and the final medication cost is not fully visible upfront. Fountain TRT : All-Inclusive Care With Direct Physician Access Best For: Patients who want bundled pricing and concierge-style text support Our Score: 4.0/5 | Trustpilot: 4.4★ (280+ reviews) Overview Fountain TRT bundles testosterone medication, labs, and physician consultations into a flat-rate subscription with concierge-style 24/7 support. The Starter plan at $199 per 4 weeks requires no upfront commitment, while the Pro plan brings the effective cost down to roughly $150 per 4 weeks with a 12-month upfront payment of $1,799. Co-founded by Dr. Doron Stember, a board-certified urologist with 10+ years in men’s health, Fountain positions itself as the concierge option in the online TRT space. The affiliated medical practice is Quaker Ridge Medical, PLLC. On Trustpilot, FountainTRT holds a 4.4-star rating across over 280 reviews, the smallest review volume on this list by a wide margin. Reviewers consistently praise the responsiveness of the care team, the quality of provider consultations, and the simplicity of the all-inclusive pricing. Negative reviews are limited but typically center on patients with complex needs feeling that Fountain’s standardized protocols don’t accommodate them. Note that Fountain operates a separate Trustpilot listing under FountainHRT (fountain.net) for its women’s hormone therapy services; the 4.4-star figure above reflects the TRT-specific listing. We did not identify a BBB listing for Fountain TRT during our review. The trade-off: Fountain offers a clean, app-based, all-inclusive experience optimized for first-time TRT patients with straightforward needs. Patients with complex hormone profiles, or who want a wider ancillary medication menu, will find Fountain’s options more limited than Defy Medical or Peter MD. The right provider depends on what you prioritize: pricing transparency, clinical depth, medication options, or care model flexibility. Male Excel stands out for its daily microdosing protocol, BBB A+ accreditation, transparent baseline pricing, and 90-day Excel Advantage Guarantee, though final medication costs depend on the prescribed dose. Regardless of which provider you choose, look for these core safeguards: blood work before any prescription, regular lab monitoring (at least every 6 months), video consultations with licensed clinicians, and a clear understanding of your total monthly cost before committing. Testosterone is a controlled substance that requires proper medical oversight. If a clinic skips baseline labs or appears to prescribe testosterone without a thorough evaluation, that is a reason to pause and ask more questions before moving forward. FAQs Do online TRT clinics require blood work before prescribing? All five providers reviewed here state that they require blood work before prescribing testosterone. This is an important part of responsible TRT care because lab results help clinicians confirm whether testosterone therapy is appropriate and monitor safety over time. If a clinic appears willing to prescribe testosterone without baseline labs or a meaningful clinical evaluation, that is a reason to pause and ask more questions before moving forward. How much do online TRT clinics cost per month? Costs vary widely depending on the provider, plan, medication, lab fees, and billing model. Among the providers reviewed here, advertised pricing ranges from Peter MD’s $79/month annual plan to Fountain TRT’s $199 per 4 weeks Starter plan. Hone Health’s TRT membership starts at $129/month, but medication is billed separately. Male Excel charges a $99/month membership plus medication costs, while Defy Medical estimates average costs of under $250/month in the first year and under $200/month after that. Always calculate the all-in cost, including labs, memberships, consultations, shipping, and medications. Are online TRT clinics legitimate? The five providers reviewed here use licensed clinicians, require lab work, and prescribe medications through partner pharmacies or pharmacy networks. However, the quality, pricing transparency, cancellation policies, and follow-up processes vary by provider. Before enrolling with any online TRT clinic, confirm that it requires blood work, clearly identifies its prescribing clinicians, explains medication sourcing, and provides transparent pricing and cancellation terms. Do any online TRT clinics accept insurance? None of the five providers reviewed here accept insurance for TRT treatment itself. However, some allow HSA, FSA, or HRA funds depending on the provider and the patient’s plan. Defy Medical also allows patients to use their own insurance for lab work through LabCorp, though reimbursement is not guaranteed. Always confirm coverage directly with your insurer or plan administrator. What is the difference between compounded and FDA-approved testosterone from online clinics? FDA-approved testosterone products have gone through FDA review for safety, effectiveness, quality, and manufacturing standards. Compounded testosterone is prepared by a compounding pharmacy for an individual patient and is not FDA-approved. Most online TRT clinics reviewed here primarily use compounded medications. Defy Medical is the only provider in this comparison confirmed to offer both compounded options and access to FDA-approved testosterone products. Can you cancel an online TRT subscription at any time? Cancellation policies vary. Hone Health and Male Excel allow cancellation of the membership, though cancellation generally applies at the end of the current billing period and fees may be non-refundable. Peter MD requires a minimum 6-month commitment on discounted plans and uses auto-renewal with a 48-hour cancellation window. Fountain TRT offers a no-commitment Starter plan, but longer plans require larger upfront payments. Defy Medical does not use a subscription model, so there is no monthly membership to cancel. Shipped medications and completed services are generally non-refundable across these providers. What red flags should you look for when choosing an online TRT clinic? Be cautious with any clinic that appears to prescribe testosterone without baseline blood work, does not clearly identify its prescribing clinicians, makes guaranteed outcome claims, or does not explain pricing and cancellation terms before payment. It is also worth asking how often follow-up labs are required, which pharmacy dispenses the medication, whether the testosterone is compounded or FDA-approved, and what happens if you need to pause, cancel, or adjust treatment. Do online TRT clinics prescribe injections, gels, or both? All five providers reviewed here offer injectable testosterone. Most also offer topical testosterone cream, which is typically compounded and is different from FDA-approved testosterone gels such as AndroGel. Traditional gel is not confirmed as a standard option for most of the providers reviewed here. Defy Medical appears to offer the broadest range of formats, including injections, topical lotions/gels, pellets, and nasal gel. Why is Policy Lab Reviewing Providers?
